{{< include ../includes/user-guide-audit.qmd >}}


Elements are named objects placed in three dimensions and assembled into a
`LINE`. Shared concepts are described once; select OPALX or OPAL above for
version-specific interfaces.

::: {.feature-opalx}


| Type | Regression use | External data |
|---|---|---|
| `DRIFT` | Field-free transport | none |
| `COLLIMATOR` | Source registered; no maintained regression input | none |
| `BOX` | Source registered; no maintained regression input | none |
| `BEAMBEAM` | [Available in OPALX V1.1.0.](#beambeam) | [optional particle input files]{#ug-12-02} |
| `CONSTANTEFIELDCAVITY` | Uniform electric field | none |
| `CONSTANTFOCUSING` | Collective linear focusing for DIH studies | none |
| `QUADRUPOLE` | Normalized quadrupole | none |
| `MULTIPOLE` | Normalized quadrupole to decapole arrays | none |
| `MULTIPOLET` | Physical multipole coefficients with fringe fields | optional time model |
| `SOLENOID` | Mapped solenoid field | field map |
| `FIELDMAP` | Static magnetic or electric field map; no maintained regression input | field map |
| `RFCAVITY` | Mapped standing-wave or ideal uniform RF field; cyclotron single-gap kick | field map or voltage profile, except for `TYPE="IDEAL"` |
| `TRAVELINGWAVE` | Traveling-wave RF field | field map |
| `CYCLOTRONSECTOR` | PSI-style cyclotron sector field | field map and optional trim coils |
| `LASER` | Source registered; `TRACK` rejects it | none |
| `MONITOR` | Source registered; no maintained regression input | output file |
| `MARKER` | Source registered; no maintained regression input | none |
| `PROBE` | Cyclotron segment recording; coasting and RF integration checks | `.h5`/`.loss`, `.hist`, `.peaks` |
| `RBEND`, `SBEND` | Source registered; no maintained regression input | none |
| `SCALINGFFAMAGNET` | Source registered; see [scaling FFA interface](#scalingffamagnet) | [optional end-field model]{#ug-12-03} |
| `VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY` | Source registered; no maintained regression input | time models |

: {tbl-colwidths="[28, 42, 30]"}

The [Element Physics](../physics/elements/index.qmd) chapter contains
derivations and benchmarks where available.

## Common element syntax {#common-element-syntax}

Every element uses

```opal
name: ELEMENTTYPE, L=length, placement, type_specific_parameters;
```

and accepts the following common attributes.

| Parameter | Default | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `L` | unset ($0\,\mathrm m$ when read) | Nominal element length. Use a positive value for the element kernels documented here. |
| `ELEMEDGE` | unset | Places the entrance at path length $s$ in metres. May be combined with `PSI`, but not with absolute pose attributes. |
| `X`, `Y`, `Z` | `0 m` | Absolute lab-frame origin. Explicitly set at least one of `X`, `Y`, `Z`, `THETA`, or `PHI` to select pose placement. |
| `THETA`, `PHI`, `PSI` | `0 rad` | Absolute rotations about local $y$, $x$, and $z$. `PSI` is also the optional roll for `ELEMEDGE` placement. |
| `DX`, `DY`, `DZ` | `0 m` | Local translational misalignment applied after placement. It moves the element for the particles only; the reference particle sees the element at its nominal place. |
| `DTHETA`, `DPHI`, `DPSI` | `0 rad` | Local rotational misalignment. |
| `APERTURE` | none | Transverse aperture string, for example `CIRCLE(0.02)`, `ELLIPSE(0.03,0.02)`, `RECTANGLE(0.03,0.02)`, or `SQUARE(0.02)`. Dimensions are full widths in metres. Other shapes and a third argument are rejected. Without it, the element has no transverse limit. See [Particle removal](#particle-removal). |
| `DELETEONTRANSVERSEEXIT` | `TRUE` | Requests particle deletion when an element reports a transverse aperture exit. |
| `TYPE` | unset | Type-specific selector, used by `RFCAVITY` and `MONITOR` below. Only listed values are accepted: `STANDING`, `SINGLEGAP` and `IDEAL` for `RFCAVITY`; `RING`, `CARBONCYCL`, `CYCIAE`, `AVFEQ`, `FFA`, `BANDRF`, `SYNCHROCYCLOTRON`, `SINGLEGAP`, `STANDING`, `TEMPORAL` and `SPATIAL` for other elements. |


: {tbl-colwidths="[28, 15, 57]"}

Exactly one placement strategy is required. Supplying both `ELEMEDGE` and an
absolute pose fails; supplying neither also fails. `PSI` alone does not select
absolute placement. All elements of one line must use the same strategy: a line
that mixes `ELEMEDGE` and absolute poses is rejected. `MARKER` is the exception;
its placement attributes are ignored.

[These placement rules have element-specific exceptions: `PROBE` uses its detector endpoints, `FIELDMAP` requires an absolute pose, and `SCALINGFFAMAGNET` uses its dedicated aperture dimensions and rejects `APERTURE`. The following sections give those interfaces.]{#ug-12-05}

### Particle removal: `APERTURE`, `COLLIMATOR`, and `BOX` {#particle-removal}

Three inputs delete particles from the beam.

| Input | Deletes particles | Where | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `APERTURE` | outside the given shape | most elements, see below | the beam pipe or the bore of a magnet or cavity |
| [`COLLIMATOR`](#collimator) | outside its `APERTURE` | a field-free element that must have `APERTURE` and `L > 0` | an aperture restriction with no field, such as an iris |
| [`BOX`](#box) | inside a block, $\lvert x\rvert <$ `WIDTH`/2 and $\lvert y\rvert <$ `HEIGHT`/2 | a field-free element, moved and tilted by its placement | a piece of material beside the beam, such as one collimator jaw |

: {tbl-colwidths="[16, 30, 27, 27]"}

`COLLIMATOR` is a `DRIFT` with an `APERTURE`; it only refuses to run without
one. `BOX` is the reverse of an aperture: the beam passes around it, not
through it.

All three follow the same rules:

- The check runs once per time step, after the particles are moved, in the
  element's local frame. Only particles with $0 \le z < L$ in that frame are
  checked.
- A particle that moves more than `L` in one step can pass an element without
  being checked. Keep the step length $\beta c\,\Delta t$ well below `L`.
- The boundary itself counts as outside: a particle exactly on it is deleted
  by `APERTURE` and `COLLIMATOR` and kept by `BOX`.
- `DELETEONTRANSVERSEEXIT=FALSE` turns deletion off for that element.
- `BOX` rejects `APERTURE`. `RBEND` and `SBEND` accept it only with `HGAP > 0`
  and a vertical half-width no larger than `HGAP`; see [bends](#bends).
  `MARKER` ignores it.
- `MULTIPOLE`, `QUADRUPOLE`, `RBEND`, `SBEND` and `RFCAVITY` with
  `TYPE="IDEAL"` apply their field only inside the aperture. With
  `DELETEONTRANSVERSEEXIT=FALSE`, a particle outside it is kept but sees no
  field from that element.
- No loss file is written. Deleted particles reduce `numParticles` in the
  `.stat` file. With `--info 2`, the log reports how many particles were
  marked for deletion in each step.

## `DRIFT` {#drift}

`DRIFT` defines a field-free interval. It advances particles only through the
normal tracker integration and provides the reference-path geometry between
active elements.

```opal
D1: DRIFT, L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.0;
```

| Parameter | Default | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `L` | unset | Drift length in metres; use a positive value. |


## `COLLIMATOR` {#collimator}

`COLLIMATOR` is a field-free element that deletes every particle outside its
`APERTURE` while the particle is inside the element body. It behaves like a
`DRIFT` with an `APERTURE`, but an input without `APERTURE` or with `L <= 0`
is rejected.

```opal
C1: COLLIMATOR, L=0.1, ELEMEDGE=1.0, APERTURE="RECTANGLE(0.02,0.01)";
```

| Parameter | Default | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `L` | required | Body length in metres; must be positive. |
| `APERTURE` | required | Opening that particles must stay inside, as described under [common element syntax](#common-element-syntax). Dimensions are full widths. |

The collimator models no material: particles are either kept or deleted.
See [Particle removal](#particle-removal) for how it differs from `BOX`.

## `BOX` {#box}

`BOX` is a field-free solid block that deletes every particle inside it. In
the element's local frame the block covers
$\lvert x\rvert <$ `WIDTH`/2, $\lvert y\rvert <$ `HEIGHT`/2, and
$0 \le z <$ `L`. Use it for material that the beam should pass around, such
as a collimator jaw.

The block is centred on its local $z$ axis. To move it beside the beam, use
the normal placement: `X`, `Y`, `Z` and the angles for pose placement, or
`DX` and `DY` with `ELEMEDGE`. This jaw covers $0 < x < 20\,\mathrm{mm}$ and
$\lvert y\rvert < 5\,\mathrm{mm}$, so the reference particle passes along its
$-x$ face:

```opal
JAW: BOX, L=0.1, X=0.01, Z=0.5, WIDTH=0.02, HEIGHT=0.01;
```

Two blocks on either side of the beam form a jaw pair. This pair leaves a
$10\,\mathrm{mm}$ horizontal gap:

```opal
JAW_L: BOX, L=0.1, X=-0.015, Z=0.5, WIDTH=0.02, HEIGHT=0.05;
JAW_R: BOX, L=0.1, X= 0.015, Z=0.5, WIDTH=0.02, HEIGHT=0.05;
```

| Parameter | Default | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `L` | required | Block length along local $z$ in metres; must be positive. |
| `WIDTH` | required | Full block width along local $x$ in metres; must be positive. |
| `HEIGHT` | required | Full block height along local $y$ in metres; must be positive. |

`BOX` does not accept `APERTURE`. OPALX treats an element as present along the
reference trajectory only where the reference particle is inside the
element's aperture, so the aperture of a block beside the beam must stay
open. The block models no material: particles are either kept or deleted.
See [Particle removal](#particle-removal) for how it differs from `APERTURE`
and `COLLIMATOR`.

## `BEAMBEAM` {#beambeam}

[**Availability:** `BEAMBEAM` is available in OPALX V1.1.0.]{#ug-12-07}

`BEAMBEAM` defines a single-pass interaction between a tracked primary bunch
and its counter-propagating mirrored primary. Selected additional particle
containers are passive witnesses: they receive the primary fields but do not
contribute charge to this interaction. The mirror is not an additional `BEAM`.

::: {.callout-important}
## Experimental, restricted collision model

Use one `BEAMBEAM` in a single-pass `LINE`, with an `OPEN` field solver.
Multiple interaction occurrences and `RING`/`TURNS` tracking are rejected.
The frozen/rigid-source approximation is intentional; this is not a general
self-consistent simulation of two independently evolving bunches.
:::

```opal
IP1: BEAMBEAM,
    L=0.32, ELEMEDGE=0.01,
    APERTURE="CIRCLE(0.30)",
    COPY_TIME=1.0e-30,
    BBRIGID=TRUE,
    WITNESS_CONTAINERS="1,2",
    VISUALIZE=FALSE;
```

This definition places the IP at $s=0.17\,\mathrm m$. The aperture diameter is
$0.30\,\mathrm m$; its radius is $0.15\,\mathrm m$. This is an element fragment:
define the beams, distributions, field solver, and `TRACK` separately.

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="BEAMBEAM parameters"}

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `L` | unset | m | Physical element length; use a positive value. The IP is its placed midpoint. |
| `COPY_TIME` | `0` | s | Positive absolute simulation-time threshold enabling the mirrored field during an active interaction. **Zero disables the mirror**, rather than activating it immediately. Negative values are rejected. |
| `BBRIGID` | `FALSE` | boolean | Suppress the primary's BeamBeam collective kick, but retain deposition and the mesh field for witnesses. Ordinary motion and external fields remain active. |
| `WITNESS_CONTAINERS` | `"NONE"` | string | Comma-separated indices in `TRACK.BEAMS`, e.g. `"1,2"`. Source index 0 is forbidden; indices must be below 53 and exist in the run. |
| `VISUALIZE` | `FALSE` | boolean | Enable the ASCII interaction-window visualization, independently of field activation. |
| `GEOMETRY` | unset | string | Accepted compatibility attribute; the current implementation does not apply a named boundary geometry through it. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[23, 12, 10, 55]"}

:::

Use a small positive `COPY_TIME` to enable the mirror at the first positive-time
active solve. `COPY`, `IP_S`, and `RETIRE_TIME` are not supported controls.

### Beams and timed witnesses {#beambeam-witnesses}

The list `BEAMS={PrimaryElectrons, WitnessElectrons, WitnessPositrons}` assigns
indices 0, 1, and 2. Define separate witness `BEAM` objects with
`PARTICLE=ELECTRON` and `PARTICLE=POSITRON` respectively, each using a distinct
distribution object. Set
`ORBITTHREADER=FALSE` on passive witness beams to reuse the primary reference-orbit
map; their physical momenta and trajectories are still independent.

Use [`EMITTEDFROMFILE`](beam-distributions.qmd#emittedfromfile) for individual
birth times. Positions are in metres, momenta in $p/(m_e c)$, and birth times in
seconds. Set the emission-source position and `T0` to align the input clock
with primary overlap at the IP. A common `FROMFILE`/`T0` injection is not
equivalent to individually timed births.

### Field region and restrictions {#beambeam-domain}

Physical length and aperture are **not** the numerical field box. The current
longitudinal field window is fixed internally to IP $\pm10$ mm. Transversely,
the mesh uses a padded, non-shrinking primary-plus-witness envelope and a
cell-aspect constraint.

For `ELEMEDGE` placement, the interaction owns collective-field policy before
the primary reaches that window: ordinary space charge is suppressed while
inactive. Once the primary tail passes the downstream boundary, the interaction
completes, witness gathering stops, and ordinary space charge remains suppressed.
Completion does not delete particles; normal transport, external fields, and
aperture handling continue.

Use `TYPE=OPEN` with open boundaries; the validated relativistic setup uses
`GREENSF=INTEGRATED` and one velocity bin. Do not combine this fixed-domain
interaction with cathode/image-charge Dirichlet planes or `FFT2D5`. A larger
physical aperture does not establish adequate field resolution. Check the
witness trajectories against the numerical longitudinal region.

`BB-DIAG` messages identify `Inactive`, `Active`, and `Completed` and report
source, copy, and witness status. Per-container outputs follow the normal
[diagnostic conventions](diagnostics-output.qmd). See
[Beam-Beam physics](../physics/beam-beam/index.qmd) for equations, the precise
activation rule, model limitations, and CAIN validation.

## `CONSTANTEFIELDCAVITY` {#constant-electric-field-cavity}

`CONSTANTEFIELDCAVITY` adds a uniform Cartesian electric field over its local
body interval. It is a DC element and is not processed by the RF autophaser.

```opal
Gun: CONSTANTEFIELDCAVITY,
    L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    EX=0.0, EY=0.0, EZ=-5.0;
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `EX` | `0` | MV/m | Uniform local $E_x$. |
| `EY` | `0` | MV/m | Uniform local $E_y$. |
| `EZ` | `0` | MV/m | Uniform local $E_z$. A negative value accelerates electrons toward local $+z$. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18, 12, 14, 56]"}

The field is applied for local $0<z\le L$ in the particle kernel. Use
`RFCAVITY` or `TRAVELINGWAVE` when an oscillating mapped RF field is required.

## `CONSTANTFOCUSING` {#constant-focusing}

`CONSTANTFOCUSING` adds linear three-dimensional focusing about the current
bunch centroid. It was introduced primarily for disorder-induced-heating (DIH)
test cases.

```opal
Focus: CONSTANTFOCUSING,
    L=1.0e-2, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    STRENGTH=1.5, RADIUS=1.774e-3;
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `STRENGTH` | `1` | none | Multiplies the initial field scale. |
| `RADIUS` | `0` | m | Reference beam radius; a positive value is required. |

On its first application, the element fixes

$$
\overline{\mathbf E}_{\mathrm{abs}}
=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}
\begin{pmatrix}|E_{i,x}|\\|E_{i,y}|\\|E_{i,z}|\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
g=\frac{\mathrm{STRENGTH}}{\mathrm{RADIUS}}
\left\lVert\overline{\mathbf E}_{\mathrm{abs}}\right\rVert_2,
$$

then adds

$$
\mathbf E_i \mathrel{+}=g\left(\mathbf R_i-\langle\mathbf R\rangle\right).
$$

The gradient $g$ remains fixed, while the bunch centroid is recomputed. The
field is applied only for element-local $0\le z<L$ and does not affect the
reference particle. With positive `STRENGTH`, it focuses electrons; the force
direction reverses with particle charge.

## `QUADRUPOLE` {#quadrupole}

`QUADRUPOLE` is a convenience wrapper around `MULTIPOLE`. It converts
normalized strengths to physical gradients with the rigidity
$B\rho = P_0/c$, where `P0` is the global reference momentum in GeV/$c$
(default 1). `P0` is not taken from `BEAM`; set it with `REAL P0 = ...;`
before the element definitions (see
[control statements](control-statements/index.qmd)).

```opal
Q1: QUADRUPOLE, L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.0, K1=0.54;
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `K1` | `0` | $\mathrm m^{-2}$ | [Normalized normal quadrupole strength.]{#ug-12-08} |
| `K1S` | `0` | $\mathrm m^{-2}$ | Skew normalized quadrupole strength. |
| `DK1` | `0` | $\mathrm m^{-2}$ | [Normal error, added to `K1` for both particles and the reference particle.]{#ug-12-09} |
| `DK1S` | `0` | $\mathrm m^{-2}$ | Skew error, added to `K1S` in the same way. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18, 12, 18, 52]"}

Use a positive `L`. Although inherited help text mentions integrated zero-length
strengths, the field is applied only on $0\le z<L$, so `L=0` gives no field.

The field does not depend on the beam's charge: the gradient is
$g = B\rho\,K_1$ for every species. A positive `K1` focuses positive particles
horizontally and defocuses negative particles horizontally.

## `MULTIPOLE` {#multipole}

`MULTIPOLE` is a straight multipole from quadrupole to decapole, defined by
arrays of normalized normal and skew strengths. Index 0 is the dipole, index 1
the quadrupole, up to index 4, the decapole.

```opal
M1: MULTIPOLE, L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.0, KN={0.0,0.54,1.2};
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `KN` | empty | $\mathrm m^{-(n+1)}$ | [Normal normalized strengths $K_n$, index $n$ from 0 (dipole) to 4 (decapole).]{#ug-12-11} |
| `KS` | empty | $\mathrm m^{-(n+1)}$ | Skew normalized strengths with the same indexing. |
| `DKN` | empty | $\mathrm m^{-(n+1)}$ | [Normal errors, added to `KN` for both particles and the reference particle. Missing entries are padded with zero.]{#ug-12-12} |
| `DKS` | empty | $\mathrm m^{-(n+1)}$ | Skew errors, added to `KS` in the same way. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[14, 12, 18, 56]"}

Each array may have at most five entries, and its first (dipole) entry must be
zero; otherwise the element is rejected. `MULTIPOLE` is placed as a straight
element, so a dipole field would steer the beam away from it. Use `SBEND` or
`RBEND` for a dipole.

[Particles and the reference particle use the same field for all orders.]{#ug-12-13} The
strengths are converted with $B\rho = P_0/c$ from the global `P0`, as for
`QUADRUPOLE`, and do not depend on the beam's charge. The field is described in
[Element Physics](../physics/elements/index.qmd#sec-elements-multipoles). As
for `QUADRUPOLE`, use positive length; `L=0` gives no field.

## `MULTIPOLET` {#multipolet}

`MULTIPOLET` defines straight or constant-radius curved magnetic multipoles
using physical field coefficients and a smooth fringe model. It is distinct
from the normalized `MULTIPOLE` interface.

```opal
MT1: MULTIPOLET,
    L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    TP={0.0,1.80},
    LFRINGE=0.05, RFRINGE=0.05,
    HAPERT=0.04, VAPERT=0.04;
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `TP` | empty | $\mathrm T\,\mathrm m^{-k}$ | Physical coefficients $b_k$: index 0 dipole field, index 1 quadrupole gradient, and higher orders through index 5. |
| `LFRINGE`, `RFRINGE` | unset | m | Left and right tanh-fringe length scales. Set positive values. |
| `HAPERT`, `VAPERT` | unset | m | Internal horizontal and vertical aperture dimensions used by this field model. |
| `MAXFORDER` | `3` | terms | Longitudinal fringe expansion order. Must be in $[1,9]$; real input is converted to an integer. |
| `MAXXORDER` | `20` | terms | Polynomial expansion order used by the curved implementation; real input is converted to an integer. |
| `ROTATION` | unset | rad | Rotation about the central axis for a straight skew element. Must be zero when `ANGLE` is nonzero. |
| `EANGLE` | unset | rad | Entrance angle for curved geometry. |
| `BBLENGTH` | unset | m | Half-length used for the field calculation's bounding region. |
| `ANGLE` | `0` | rad | Nonzero selects the constant-radius curved implementation; zero selects straight geometry. |
| `VARRADIUS` | `FALSE` | Boolean | [Variable-radius selector. Variable-radius curved magnets are currently rejected.]{#ug-12-14} |
| `ENTRYOFFSET` | `0` | m | Accepted only with `VARRADIUS=TRUE`; there is no supported variable-radius curved configuration yet. |
| `SCALING_MODEL` | unset | name | Optional `TIMEDEPENDENCE` object multiplying the magnetic field as a function of time. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20, 12, 15, 53]"}

The dedicated `HAPERT` and `VAPERT` values configure this model's internal
aperture; do not substitute the common `APERTURE` string for them. The six-entry
`TP` capacity is a runtime limit even though the parser accepts a longer array.

## `SOLENOID` {#solenoid}

[**UG-12-15:** `SOLENOID` loads a magnetic field map. The current mapped-field calculation multiplies the loaded field directly by `KS` (and by `KS+DKS` for tracked particles), despite the normalized-strength wording in the input help. The map defines the actual longitudinal field-support interval, which may differ from nominal `L`.]{.ug-audit-other #ug-12-15}

```opal
S1: SOLENOID,
    L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    KS=0.12, FMAPFN="solenoid.T7";
```

| Parameter | Default | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `KS` | unset ($0$ when read) | [**UG-12-16:** Direct multiplier on the loaded magnetic field in the current mapped-field calculation. Check the map normalization; the input-help label $\mathrm m^{-1}$ does not describe the applied scale.]{.ug-audit-other #ug-12-16} |
| `DKS` | unset ($0$ when read) | Additive scale error for tracked particles; the reference-particle field omits this error. |
| `FMAPFN` | unset | Required field-map filename. Tracking cannot apply a solenoid without a loaded map. |
| `FAST` | `TRUE` | Parsed but not used. |
| `ZREVERSE` | `FALSE` | [Reverse the map longitudinally and negate its longitudinal magnetic field. Supported only by G4beamline `cylinder` maps; see [field-map restrictions](appendix/field-maps/index.qmd#opalx-g4bl-cylinder).]{#ug-12-17} |

The element does not generate an analytic hard-edge solenoid when `FMAPFN` is
missing. Keep the field map beside the input or use an unambiguous relative
path.

## `FIELDMAP` {#fieldmap}

`FIELDMAP` places a static field map in the lattice. The map can hold a
magnetic field, an electric field, or both. The element has no field of its
own: the field comes from the map, and the map's z range sets the element's
start and length.

The element's local frame is the map's own coordinate frame. The 6D pose
places the map's origin, which need not be the start of the map.

```opal
ASR61: FIELDMAP,
    X=0.0699, Y=0.0, Z=2.9745,
    THETA=0.349066, PHI=0.0, PSI=0.0,
    FMAPFN="asr61_300d_track.g4blmap", BSCALE=-0.99528;
```

This places a G4beamline [`grid` map](appendix/field-maps/index.qmd#opalx-g4bl-grid)
of a bending magnet with its origin at the given lab point, rotated by
$20^\circ$ about $y$. The map covers $z=-1.38$ to $+1.38\,\mathrm m$ in its own
frame, so the element starts $1.38\,\mathrm m$ before its origin and is
$2.76\,\mathrm m$ long. The field is the map times $-0.99528$.

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="FIELDMAP parameters"}

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `FMAPFN` | unset | path | Required static field map. Accepted types are `2DMagnetoStatic`, `AstraMagnetoStatic`, and G4beamline [`cylinder`](appendix/field-maps/index.qmd#opalx-g4bl-cylinder) and [`grid`](appendix/field-maps/index.qmd#opalx-g4bl-grid) maps. Time-dependent maps are rejected; use `RFCAVITY` or `TRAVELINGWAVE` for those. |
| `BSCALE` | `1` | none | Multiplier on the magnetic field. G4beamline maps are read in tesla as written, so `1` reproduces the map; this is the `current=` given where G4beamline places the map. `2DMagnetoStatic` and `AstraMagnetoStatic` maps are normalized to an on-axis peak of `1 T` unless their header turns that off; for them `BSCALE` is the peak field in tesla. |
| `ESCALE` | `1` | none | Multiplier on the electric field, for a map that holds one (currently G4beamline `grid` maps only). This is the `gradient=` given where G4beamline places the map. No effect on a map without an electric field. |
| `ZREVERSE` | `FALSE` | Boolean | Mirror the map in z and negate the longitudinal field, as when the magnet is turned around. This is G4beamline's `rotation=Y180`. Only G4beamline `cylinder` maps accept it. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[16, 10, 10, 64]"}

:::

Restrictions:

- Place `FIELDMAP` with a 6D pose (`X`, `Y`, `Z`, `THETA`, `PHI`, `PSI`).
  `ELEMEDGE` is rejected. A line uses one placement form, so every other
  element in the line must use a 6D pose too.
- `L` is rejected; the length comes from the map.
- A particle outside the map's transverse range gets no field from it. This is
  not counted as a loss; use `APERTURE` to remove particles.
- `APERTURE` is checked over the map's z range.
- `AstraMagnetoStatic` maps have no transverse range. Give an `APERTURE` if the
  beam can leave the region the map describes.
- A file is loaded once per run, so one file cannot be used with both
  `ZREVERSE` settings in the same run.
- `COF` and localized `TURNS` do not accept `FIELDMAP`.
- Every MPI rank holds its own copy of the map. See
  [memory use](appendix/field-maps/index.qmd#opalx-g4bl-grid-memory) for the
  size of a `grid` map.

## `RFCAVITY` {#rfcavity}

`RFCAVITY` selects an RF model with `TYPE`:

- `STANDING` (default): a standing-wave field from a dynamic field map.
- `IDEAL`: a uniform longitudinal RF field over the element length, without
  a field map.
- `SINGLEGAP`: a discrete cyclotron voltage-profile kick, described in
  [Accelerated Beam](cyclotron.qmd#accelerated-beam).

The parameters below describe `STANDING` and `IDEAL`. The
[autophased mapped example](../getting-started/worked-inputs.qmd#example-rfcavity)
shows the complete connection to a beam and tracker.

```opal
Gun: RFCAVITY,
    L=0.2927, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    TYPE="STANDING", VOLT=60.0,
    FREQ=1300.0, LAG=0.0,
    FMAPFN="fieldmaps/DriveGun.T7";
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `TYPE` | unset (`STANDING` behavior) | name | Accepted values are `STANDING`, `SINGLEGAP`, and `IDEAL`. Other input values are rejected. |
| `L` | unset | m | `IDEAL` requires a finite positive length and applies its field on local $0\le z<L$. |
| `VOLT`, `DVOLT` | unset | MV/m | Nominal peak electric-field amplitude and additive amplitude error for `IDEAL`; field-map amplitude and additive amplitude error for `STANDING`. |
| `FREQ` | unset | MHz | RF frequency. For `STANDING`, a field-map value differing by more than 1% replaces it with a warning. `IDEAL` requires a finite, nonnegative value; zero selects a static field. |
| `LAG`, `DLAG` | unset | rad | Nominal phase and additive phase error, using a cosine convention. |
| `FMAPFN` | unset | path | Required for `STANDING`; supported maps are `FM2DDynamic`, `FM3DDynamic`, and `Astra1DDynamic`. Must be omitted for `IDEAL`. |
| `FAST` | `TRUE` | Boolean | Parsed but not used. |
| `APVETO` | `FALSE` | Boolean | If true, excludes this cavity from automatic phase optimization. |
| `DESIGNENERGY` | `-1` | MeV | Positive target exit kinetic energy; the autophaser also adjusts amplitude to reach it. Negative disables the target. |
| `GEOMETRY` | unset | name | [Parsed boundary-geometry compatibility attribute; not connected by the current element update.]{#ug-12-18} |
| `RMIN`, `RMAX`, `ANGLE`, `PDIS`, `GAPWIDTH`, `PHI0` | unset | model-specific | Used by the separate `SINGLEGAP` interface; see the cyclotron guide. They do not configure the `STANDING` or `IDEAL` field. |
| `PHASE_MODEL`, `AMPLITUDE_MODEL`, `FREQUENCY_MODEL` | unset | name | [Rejected for `IDEAL`. For `STANDING`, names are stored but not resolved into time-dependence objects. Use `VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY` when RF parameters must vary with time.]{#ug-12-19} |

: {tbl-colwidths="[24, 12, 15, 49]"}

The instantaneous electric map scale uses the configured amplitude and
$\cos(2\pi f t+\mathrm{LAG})$; the magnetic map component uses the corresponding
sine factor. `OPTION.AUTOPHASE>0` searches the reference-particle phase for
maximum exit energy, using the option value as the number of refinement passes.
This also applies to `IDEAL`, including amplitude adjustment when
`DESIGNENERGY>0`. Set `APVETO=TRUE` to retain the specified phase, or
[`OPTION, AUTOPHASE=0;` to disable the normal phase search. To preserve a cavity phase also during advancement to `TRACK.ZSTART`, set `APVETO=TRUE` on that cavity; the global option is not honored during that initial advancement.]{#ug-12-20}

### Ideal uniform RF field {#rfcavity-ideal}

```opal
RF1: RFCAVITY,
    TYPE="IDEAL", L=0.2, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    VOLT=5.0, FREQ=100.0, LAG=0.0,
    APVETO=TRUE;
```

Here `VOLT=5.0` sets a peak longitudinal field of 5 MV/m. With `L=0.2`,
the peak integrated voltage is $5.0\times0.2=1$ MV. At fixed `VOLT`, changing
`L` changes the field extent and integrated voltage. The field is uniform
transversely inside `APERTURE` and zero outside the cavity's longitudinal
interval. Without `APERTURE`,
there is no transverse field limit. The model adds no magnetic field, fringe
fields, or transverse RF focusing.

With $t$ in seconds, the longitudinal field inside the cavity is

$$
E_z(t)=10^6(\mathrm{VOLT}+\mathrm{DVOLT})
\cos\!\left(2\pi\,10^6\mathrm{FREQ}\,t+\mathrm{LAG}+\mathrm{DLAG}\right)
\quad[\mathrm{V/m}].
$$

The reference particle uses the nominal `VOLT` and `LAG`, excluding `DVOLT`
and `DLAG`. All RF parameters must be finite. `FMAPFN` and named time models
are not accepted. The nominal peak integrated voltage is `VOLT` times `L`
in MV; the actual energy gain also depends on charge, RF phase, and transit
time through the cavity.

`VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY` instead takes an amplitude model in MV/m and uses a sine
phase convention. For constant parameters and zero errors, the corresponding
amplitude is `VOLT` and its phase is `LAG` plus $\pi/2$.
See the [ideal RF field model](../physics/elements/index.qmd#ideal-rfcavity-model)
for sampling and transit-time details.

## `TRAVELINGWAVE` {#travelingwave}

`TRAVELINGWAVE` applies a mapped traveling-wave RF structure. It shares the
autophase controls with `RFCAVITY` and additionally describes the repeated-cell
geometry.

```opal
TW1: TRAVELINGWAVE,
    L=2.8, ELEMEDGE=0.5,
    VOLT=15.0, FREQ=2998.0, LAG=0.0,
    FMAPFN="traveling-wave.T7",
    NUMCELLS=84, MODE=0.3333333333;
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `VOLT`, `DVOLT` | unset | MV/m | Nominal field-map amplitude and additive error. |
| `FREQ` | unset | MHz | RF frequency converted internally to angular frequency. |
| `LAG`, `DLAG` | unset | rad | Nominal phase and additive phase error. |
| `FMAPFN` | unset | path | Required traveling-wave field map. It must be an `Astra1DDynamic` map whose $z$ range starts at 0. |
| `FAST` | `TRUE` | Boolean | Parsed but not used. |
| `APVETO` | `FALSE` | Boolean | Excludes the structure from automatic phase optimization when true. |
| `NUMCELLS` | unset | cells | Number of cells, converted from real input to an integer. Use a positive integer. |
| `MODE` | `1/3` | turns | RF phase advance between neighboring cells, expressed as a fraction of $2\pi$. |
| `DESIGNENERGY` | `-1` | MeV | [Positive autophaser target exit kinetic energy; negative disables the target. Traveling-wave target-energy tuning is incomplete; do not rely on it to set a consistent field amplitude throughout the structure.]{#ug-12-21} |

: {tbl-colwidths="[20, 12, 15, 53]"}

Use a regression-matched map, cell count, and mode as one consistent set. As
[with `RFCAVITY`, use `APVETO=TRUE` to preserve this element's prescribed phase, including advancement to `TRACK.ZSTART`. `AUTOPHASE=0` disables the normal search but is not honored during that initial advancement.]{#ug-12-22}

## `CYCLOTRONSECTOR` {#cyclotronsector}

`CYCLOTRONSECTOR` loads a PSI median-plane magnetic sector map and applies it as
one explicitly placed sector of a cyclotron `RING`. It may reference named
`TRIMCOIL` definitions that add full-azimuth radial correction fields.

```opal
TC1: TRIMCOIL, TYPE="PSI-BFIELD-MIRRORED",
     RMIN=4.350, RMAX=4.470, BMAX=1.4E-3, SLPTC=600.0;

SM0: CYCLOTRONSECTOR, FMAPFN="bfield.dat", SYM=8,
     RMIN=1.9, RMAX=4.7, VMIN=-0.05, VMAX=0.05,
     BSCALE=1, TRIMCOIL={"TC1"}, X=3.3, Y=0, Z=0, THETA=0;
```

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `FMAPFN` | unset | path | Required PSI sector field-map filename. |
| `SYM` | `8` | count | Integer sector symmetry; must be at least 2 and match the map span. |
| `RMIN`, `RMAX` | map bounds | m | Optional bounds. If supplied, they must match the field-map radii. |
| `VMIN`, `VMAX` | `-0.05`, `0.05` | m | Vertical support range for field evaluation. |
| `BSCALE` | `1` | none | Multiplier applied to the base sector map. |
| `TRIMCOIL` | empty | names | String array naming previously defined `TRIMCOIL` objects. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18, 12, 12, 58]"}

A `TRIMCOIL` definition currently supports `TYPE="PSI-BFIELD-MIRRORED"` with
finite SI parameters `0<RMIN<RMAX`, `BMAX` in tesla, and positive `SLPTC` in
inverse metres. The trim-coil profile has tails; `RMIN` and `RMAX` describe the
shape radii, not hard field-support cutoffs.

Use explicit absolute placement for each sector occurrence. The common
`ELEMEDGE` placement form is not appropriate for cyclotron sectors in new input
files.

## `LASER` {#laser}

`LASER` defines an analytic laser pulse. The definition is accepted, but a
`TRACK` whose line contains a `LASER` stops with the error
`Tracking of the "LASER" element is not implemented yet.`

```opal
L1: LASER, L=0.0, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
    WAVELENGTH=800e-9, PULSEENERGY=1.0,
    PULSELENGTH=30e-15, WAISTX=20e-6, WAISTY=20e-6,
    DIR={0,0,-1}, STOKES={1,0,0};
```

| Parameter | Unit | Constraint |
|---|---:|---|
| `WAVELENGTH` | m | Required and greater than zero. |
| `PULSEENERGY` | J | Required and greater than zero. |
| `PULSELENGTH` | s | Required and greater than zero. |
| `WAISTX`, `WAISTY` | m | Required and greater than zero. |
| `DIR` | none | Required nonzero three-vector; OPALX normalizes it. |
| `STOKES` | none | Optional three-vector with $\xi_1^2+\xi_2^2+\xi_3^2\le1$. |
| `L` | m | Optional non-negative body length. |

## `MONITOR` {#monitor}

`MONITOR` samples the bunch at a placed diagnostic plane. It adds no field and
does not remove the particles it records.

```opal
M1: MONITOR, L=0.01, ELEMEDGE=0.5, TYPE=SPATIAL, OUTFN="monitor.h5";
```

| Parameter | Default | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `L` | at least `0.01` m at update | Element geometry length. Sampling takes place at the local $z=0$ plane, rather than throughout this length. |
| `TYPE` | spatial collection | `TEMPORAL` selects a bunch snapshot triggered by the reference crossing; `SPATIAL`, another value from the common `TYPE` list, or no value selects individual spatial crossings. Values outside that list are rejected. Use `SPATIAL` explicitly for clarity. |
| `OUTFN` | element name | Output stem. A supplied extension is stripped before `.h5` or `.loss` is added. |

The monitor accepts the common placement attributes. Its sampling plane is the
origin of the placed element frame. Increasing `L` does not average the bunch
over a thicker detector.

### Spatial and temporal sampling {#monitor-collection-modes}

| Mode | What is sampled | Longitudinal interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| `SPATIAL` | Each particle's forward crossing of the monitor plane, estimated by a straight drift with its current momentum. | Records lie at local $z=0$, at different arrival times. |
| `TEMPORAL` | The primary container's particles, drifted to a common snapshot when the reference particle crosses the plane. | Particles retain longitudinal offsets within the bunch; they need not lie on the plane. |

For positive timesteps, spatial sampling requires a strict negative-to-positive
crossing in local $z$. A state exactly on either predicted endpoint is not
selected by this test. The monitor retains the current momentum; there is no
additional field integration to the crossing. See the
[MONITOR sampling model](../physics/elements/index.qmd#monitor-sampling-model)
for the intersection and drift formulas.

Spatial records use the monitor-local coordinates. Temporal positions use a
reference-aligned snapshot frame, while the stored momenta and spins are taken
from the current particle container, along the bunch-frame axes. These records should not be interpreted as
laboratory coordinates without accounting for the corresponding frame.

### Output files and timestamps {#monitor-output-times}

With `OPTION, ASCIIDUMP=FALSE, ENABLEHDF5=TRUE`, the particle file is
`<OUTFN>.h5`. With `ASCIIDUMP=TRUE`, it is `<OUTFN>.loss`, an ASCII file with
position, normalized momentum, particle ID and time. The `.loss` extension
comes from the shared output writer; monitor records are sampled particles,
not particle losses.

HDF5 particle datasets include `id`, `x`, `y`, `z`, `px`, `py`, `pz`, `q`,
`m`, and `time`. Positions use metres, normalized momentum is dimensionless,
and times use seconds. For a beam with `POLARIZATION`, the HDF5 file also
holds `polx`, `poly` and `polz`, and the ASCII file adds the columns `polx`,
`poly` and `polz` after `time`. The recorded spin is the value at the start of
the crossing step; it is not turned to the crossing time. See
[Spin Tracking](../physics/spin-tracking/index.qmd). Each saved set also carries reference `TIME`, mean
particle time `meanTime`, and time spread `rmsTime`.

| HDF5 quantity | `SPATIAL` | Current `TEMPORAL` convention |
|---|---|---|
| `TIME` | Reference particle's estimated crossing time. | Reference crossing time, corresponding to the drifted snapshot positions. |
| Particle `time` | Individual estimated crossing time. | Bunch timestep-end time, shared by the snapshot's particle records. |
| `meanTime` | Mean of the particle crossing times. | Mean of the saved particle timestamps, hence the timestep-end time. |
| `rmsTime` | Spread of the particle crossing times. | Zero for a snapshot with one common saved timestamp; it is not the bunch arrival-time spread. |

The temporal timestamp distinction is retained for legacy compatibility:
`TIME` and particle `time` / `meanTime` can differ. Use `TIME` to identify the
instant represented by the temporal snapshot positions. For example, a
reference crossing at 267.543 ps during a timestep ending at 270 ps can produce
positions for 267.543 ps and particle timestamps of 270 ps.

The modes also retain different legacy mass and energy conventions. The HDF5
`m`, `TotalMass`, and `ENERGY` values should not be compared between spatial
and temporal records as if they represented the same physical quantities.
This distinction does not change the dimensionless momentum components.

The [moment and emittance definitions](conventions/index.qmd#bunch-moments-emittance)
explain the population averages and projected RMS estimators. Applied to
spatial records, the $(z,\widetilde p_z)$ emittance is approximately zero because the
sampled positions lie on one plane; use the crossing-time distribution for
longitudinal arrival information.

## `MARKER` {#marker}

`MARKER` identifies a lattice location without adding a field. It accepts the
common placement attributes but ignores them: a `MARKER` is not placed and
does nothing during tracking. Built-in `#S` and `#E` markers denote the start
and end of a line.

```opal
IP: MARKER;
```

## `PROBE` {#probe}

`PROBE` records crossings of a finite cyclotron detector segment without removing
particles or changing their integration steps. Include it in the tracked `LINE`
or `RING` together with the `CYCLOTRONSECTOR` elements.

```opal
P1: PROBE, XSTART=1900, XEND=4700, YSTART=0, YEND=0,
    STEP=1, OUTFN="radial-probe";
```

| Parameter | Unit | Behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `XSTART`, `XEND` | mm | Segment endpoint laboratory **X** coordinates. |
| `YSTART`, `YEND` | mm | Segment endpoint laboratory **Z** coordinates (legacy cyclotron names). |
| `STEP` | mm | Positive finite radial histogram bin width; default `1`. |
| `WIDTH` | — | Legacy attribute, unused. |
| `OUTFN` | path | Output basename; defaults to the element name. A supplied extension is removed. |

The OPALX cyclotron machine plane is laboratory X–Z; laboratory Y is vertical
and is unrestricted by the probe. Endpoints are global laboratory coordinates,
independent of the containing sequence's pose. `L`, `ELEMEDGE` and the common
placement attributes do not position the probe. Endpoints must be finite and
distinct. Histograms are limited to 10 million bins per probe.

Both crossing directions are recorded; segment endpoints are included. A
particle initially on the detector is not recorded until it leaves and returns.
A 1 nm excursion from the detector plane arms the next crossing and suppresses
near-plane jitter. Crossings are interpolated between accepted particle states.
Choose `DT` small enough to resolve each crossing and keep the probe away from
RF kick planes; see [crossing accuracy](../physics/overview/index.qmd#cyclotron-probe-diagnostics).

For basename `radial-probe`, the outputs are:

- `radial-probe.h5`, or `radial-probe.loss` with `OPTION, ASCIIDUMP=TRUE`:
  particle ID, laboratory position [m], mechanical momentum normalized by
  $mc$, crossing time [s], zero-based reference turn and container (`bunchNumber`).
  HDF5 also stores particle charge [C] and mass [GeV/$c^2$].
- `radial-probe.hist`: counts in radial bins, with bounds and bin width in mm.
  Radius is measured from the laboratory origin in the X–Z plane.
- `radial-probe.peaks`: mean crossing radius [mm] for each reference turn with
  hits, in increasing turn order. These are radial means, not fitted histogram
  peak locations. Hits from multiple containers with the same turn are pooled.

Accepted probe hits are flushed collectively every 100 tracking steps and at
normal completion. HDF5/ASCII records are appended; `.hist` and `.peaks` remain
cumulative summaries. A collectively reported SINGLEGAP transport error flushes
previously accepted crossings before aborting; the failed step is not recorded.
A hard process termination can still lose the unflushed batch. Periodic flushing
does not enable checkpoint restart.

A run without hits writes a zero histogram and header-only `.peaks`, and no
phase-space file. Probe output basenames must be unique within a run; existing probe output files
are rejected, so use a fresh basename for each run. Recording
supports particle sorting and MPI migration, including empty ranks. It does not
relax existing restrictions of the SINGLEGAP cyclotron transport model.
 An independent fresh `TRACK` run starts a new recording and
requires fresh output basenames. Legacy FFA/RingElement probe placement remains a separate feature. `COF`
currently requires a field-only lattice without `PROBE`; use a separate `RING`
for the orbit solve. A newly emitted particle begins its crossing history at its
first accepted endpoint; no crossing is inferred across an unobserved interval.

## `RBEND` and `SBEND` {#bends}

`RBEND` defines rectangular bend geometry whose `L` is the straight body
length. `SBEND` defines sector geometry whose `L` is the design-orbit arc
length. Both apply normal and skew dipole and quadrupole fields.

```opal
REAL P0 = 0.1;   // GeV/c, reference momentum for the strengths
B1: SBEND, L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=1.0, ANGLE=0.1,
    K1=0.0, HGAP=0.02, FINT=0.5;
```

| Parameter | Unit | Current behavior |
|---|---:|---|
| `ANGLE` | rad | Bend angle of the design orbit. |
| `K0`, `K0S` | $\mathrm m^{-1}$ | Normal and skew dipole strengths. If `K0` is omitted, it is derived from `ANGLE`: `ANGLE/L` for `SBEND`, $2\sin(\mathrm{ANGLE}/2)/L$ for `RBEND` (`ANGLE` divided by the arc length when `E1` or `E2` is given). A given `K0` replaces this value. |
| `K1`, `K1S` | $\mathrm m^{-2}$ | Normal and skew quadrupole strengths. |
| `K2`, `K2S`, `K3`, `K3S` | $\mathrm m^{-3}$, $\mathrm m^{-4}$ | Parsed but not applied: the field has dipole and quadrupole terms only. |
| `HGAP` | m | Half gap, default 0. `HGAP > 0` gives an Enge fringe field reaching five full gaps past each face and a vertical aperture of $\pm$`HGAP`. `HGAP = 0` gives a hard edge and no aperture. |
| `FINT` | none | Fringe integral, default `0.5`. Used only with `HGAP > 0`, for the vertical edge focusing. |
| `HAPERT` | m | Horizontal half-aperture. Must be positive, needs `HGAP > 0`, and cannot be combined with `APERTURE`. |
| `E1`, `E2` | [rad]{.ug-audit-availability} | [**UG-12-24:** `RBEND` only: entrance and exit pole-face angles, default `ANGLE/2` each. They must satisfy `E1 + E2 = ANGLE`; give one and the other is derived. Each must lie strictly between $-\pi/2$ and $\pi/2$. `SBEND` rejects them.]{.ug-audit-availability #ug-12-24} |
| `FMAPFN` | path | `RBEND` only: a `1DProfile1` fringe-profile file, or `"1DPROFILE1-DEFAULT"` for OPAL's default profile. The dipole is then calibrated to `ANGLE`; `K0`…`K3S` and `FINT` are rejected. `SBEND` ignores it. |
| `DESIGNENERGY` | MeV | `RBEND` only: kinetic energy the field is set for. The field is scaled by $p(\mathrm{DESIGNENERGY})/P_0$. Must be positive. `SBEND` rejects it. |
| `H1`, `H2` | $\mathrm m^{-1}$ | Pole-face curvature: rejected by `RBEND`, ignored by `SBEND`. |
| `GAP`, `GREATERTHANPI` | [m / —]{.ug-audit-availability} | [`GAP` is the full gap for `RBEND`, instead of `HGAP`; giving both is rejected. `SBEND` rejects `GAP`. `GREATERTHANPI` is rejected by `SBEND` and ignored by `RBEND`.]{.ug-audit-availability} |
| `SLICES`, `STEPSIZE` | - | Parsed but not used. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[22, 14, 64]"}

The strengths are converted with $B\rho = P_0/c$ from the global `P0`
(GeV/$c$, default 1), as for `QUADRUPOLE`; set `P0` to the beam's reference
momentum. Unlike `MULTIPOLE`, the bend divides the field by the charge of the
beam, so the bend direction is the same for either sign of charge.

`APERTURE` is accepted only with `HGAP > 0`, and its vertical half-width must not
exceed `HGAP`. Particles are removed only inside the body, $0\le s<L$, while the
field also acts in the fringe regions.

The classes are registered but currently lack maintained regression inputs.
Treat pole-face, fringe, aperture, and sign conventions as experimental until
validated for the intended lattice. See
[Element Physics](../physics/elements/index.qmd#sec-elements-bends) for the
field model.

## `SCALINGFFAMAGNET` {#scalingffamagnet}

`SCALINGFFAMAGNET` defines a horizontal fixed-field alternating-gradient magnet.

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `B0` | T |   | Nominal dipole field at zero height. |
| `R0` | m |   | Radial scale $R_0$. If positive, curvature is towards negative x i.e. anticlockwise. If negative, curvature is towards positive x i.e. clockwise. |
| `FIELD_INDEX` |  |  | The scaling magnet field index $k$. |
| `TAN_DELTA` |  | 0 | Spiral factor $\tan(\delta)$. |
| `MAX_Y_POWER` | integer | 3 | [Maximum power of $y$ in the field expansion, limited to 20; real input is rounded down to an integer.]{#ug-12-25} |
| `FRINGE_LENGTH` | m | 0.1 | Exponential decay constant for the fringe field. |
| `RADIAL_NEG_EXTENT` | m | 1 | Field width, from the reference point towards the middle of the ring. |
| `RADIAL_POS_EXTENT` | m | 1 | Field width, from the reference point towards the outside of the ring. |
| `HEIGHT` | m | 1 | Full height of the field element. |
| `AZIMUTHAL_EXTENT` | m | * | Field map cut off in $\psi$ direction from the element centre. [Without a named end-field model, the default is `L/2 + 5*FRINGE_LENGTH`; with a named model, it is derived from that model's centre and fringe lengths.]{#ug-12-26} |
| `END_FIELD_MODEL` | |  | If set, enables a field model plugin like ENGE function. Set to the name of the EndFieldModel element. |


The `SCALINGFFAMAGNET` element defines a FFA scaling magnet. Horizontal scaling
FFA magnets are defined having a field on the midplane given by

$B_y = B_0(\psi) \left(\frac{r}{R_0}\right)^k$

where $\psi$ is an azimuthal coordinate in the spiral coordinate system, given by

$\psi = \phi - tan(\delta) \ln\left(\frac{r}{R_0}\right)$

Normally horizontal FFAs are circular so ScalingFFAMagnet elements are placed
using `ELEMEDGE` on a circle of radius `R0` with `ELEMEDGE` = 0.0
corresponding to (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0). If `R0` is positive, the placements
will have an anticlockwise arrangement; the ring curves towards the negative x
direction. If `R0` is negative, placements will have a clockwise arrangement.

In FFAs the fringe field is particularly important. By default ScalingFFAMagnet
applies a `tanh` fringe field. The e-fold length of the tanh function is defined
by `FRINGE_LENGTH` parameter. Note that if the `FRINGE_LENGTH` is comparable to
`L`, the field at the magnet centre may never reach `B0`; the magnet in this
case is fringe-field dominated. The `END_FIELD_MODEL` parameter is a string that
[selects a named model such as an Enge function. This model
replaces the default tanh model and supersedes both `L` and `FRINGE_LENGTH`.
See End Field Models below for options.]{#ug-12-27}

A diagram of the field generated by a `SCALINGFFAMAGNET` is shown below.

![FFA Field Map showing geometrical interpretation of commands. Note that POS
and NEG are abbreviations for RADIAL_POS_EXTENT and RADIAL_NEG_EXTENT
respectively](figures/scalingffa_fieldmap_xz.png)

This field map was generated from:

```opal
FFAMagnet : SCALINGFFAMAGNET, L=0.5, ELEMEDGE=0.5,
            B0=+1.0, R0=R0, FIELD_INDEX=1, TAN_DELTA=0.0, MAX_Y_POWER=5,
            FRINGE_LENGTH=0.05,
            RADIAL_NEG_EXTENT=0.2, RADIAL_POS_EXTENT=0.4, HEIGHT=0.5;
```


## End Field models

ScalingFFAMagnets use plugin end field models to determine the shape of the
fringe field, smoothly varying into the body of the element. Three models are
implemented:

* Tanh
* Enge
* AsymmetricEnge

The model's name is used as a string unique identifier to identify it for later
lookup by a field element.

### `TANH`

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `LENGTH` | m |   | Length of the field model $L$. |
| `FRINGE_LENGTH` | m |   | E-fold distance $\lambda_f$. |

`TANH` end field model generates an end field like

$f(x) = tanh\left( \frac{x+L/2}{\lambda_f} \right)/2-tanh\left( \frac{x-L/2}{\lambda_f} \right)/2$

This is implemented in ScalingFFAMagnet by default.

### `ENGE`

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `LENGTH` | m |   | Length of the field model $L$. |
| `FRINGE_LENGTH` | m |   | E-fold distance $\lambda_f$. |
| `COEFFICIENTS` |  |   | Polynomial coefficients $c_n$. |

Enge end field model generates an end field like

[**UG-12-28:** $f(x) = \frac{1}{1+e^{p(-x - L/2)}}+\frac{1}{1+e^{p(x - L/2)}} - 1$]{.ug-audit-other #ug-12-28}

where $p(x)$ is a polynomial like

$p(x) = c_0 + c_1 \left(\frac{x}{\lambda_f}\right) + c_2 \left(\frac{x}{\lambda_f}\right)^2 + \ldots$


### `ASYMMETRIC_ENGE`

| Parameter | Unit | Default | Meaning |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `START_HALF_LENGTH` | [m]{.ug-audit-other} |  | [**UG-12-29:** Entrance half-length offset $L_s$.]{.ug-audit-other #ug-12-29} |
| `START_FRINGE_LENGTH` | m |   | E-fold distance $\lambda_s,f$. |
| `START_COEFFICIENTS` |  |   | List of polynomial coefficients $c_s,n$. |
| `END_HALF_LENGTH` | [m]{.ug-audit-other} |  | [**UG-12-30:** Exit half-length offset $L_e$.]{.ug-audit-other #ug-12-30} |
| `END_FRINGE_LENGTH` | m |   | E-fold distance for the end field $\lambda_e,f$. |
| `END_COEFFICIENTS` |  |   | List of polynomial coefficients for the end field $c_e,n$. |

`ASYMMETRIC_ENGE` end field model generates an end field like

[**UG-12-31:** $f(x) = \frac{1}{1+e^{p_s(-x - L_s)}}+\frac{1}{1+e^{p_e(x - L_e)}} - 1$]{.ug-audit-other #ug-12-31}

where $p_s(x)$ is a polynomial like

$p_s(x) = c_s,0 + c_s,1 \left(\frac{x}{\lambda_s,f}\right) + c_s,2 \left(\frac{x}{\lambda_s,f}\right)^2 + \ldots$

$p_e(x) = c_e,0 + c_e,1 \left(\frac{x}{\lambda_e,f}\right) + c_e,2 \left(\frac{x}{\lambda_e,f}\right)^2 + \ldots$


## `VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY` {#variable-rf-cavity}

`VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY` applies an ideal, spatially uniform longitudinal electric
field within a finite rectangular cavity. Named time-dependence definitions
supply its amplitude, frequency, and explicit phase. It is registered for
ordinary `PARALLEL` particle tracking and compatible analytic `RING` tracking,
including the `TURNS` stopping condition.

```opal
Amplitude: POLYNOMIAL_TIME_DEPENDENCE, P0=0.05;  // MV/m
Frequency: POLYNOMIAL_TIME_DEPENDENCE, P0=3.0;   // MHz
Phase: POLYNOMIAL_TIME_DEPENDENCE, P0=0.0;       // rad
VC1: VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY, L=0.2, ELEMEDGE=0.0,
     PHASE_MODEL=Phase, AMPLITUDE_MODEL=Amplitude,
     FREQUENCY_MODEL=Frequency, WIDTH=0.1, HEIGHT=0.1,
     APERTURE="RECTANGLE(0.1,0.1)";
```

| Parameter | Expected model output |
|---|---|
| `PHASE_MODEL` | Phase in radians. |
| `AMPLITUDE_MODEL` | Electric field in MV/m. |
| `FREQUENCY_MODEL` | Frequency in MHz. |
| `WIDTH`, `HEIGHT`, `L` | Full cavity dimensions in metres. `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` are required; zero or unset values are rejected when tracking starts. |

The field support is $0\le z<L$, $|x|\le\mathrm{WIDTH}/2$, and
$|y|\le\mathrm{HEIGHT}/2$ in the element frame. The entrance and transverse
faces are included; the longitudinal exit is excluded. Outside this support
the cavity adds no field. `WIDTH` and `HEIGHT` define field support; the
generic `APERTURE` independently controls particle-loss checks. Set it
explicitly when aperture losses should use the same dimensions.

The time models receive the physical time in **seconds**. Device particle
fields and host reference fields use the same Boris midpoint time,
$t+\Delta t/2$, for each accepted step. The cavity adds only local $E_z$;
it has no fringe fields or transverse RF focusing. Its phase is not changed
by automatic cavity phasing. For a stationary bunch, choose the RF harmonic
from the measured reference return time and set each cavity's phase using
its actual transit time; a zero field at the entrance does not establish
zero net energy gain through a finite cavity. See the
[RF field model](../physics/elements/index.qmd#variable-rf-cavity-model).

`COF` remains a fixed-energy static magnetic calculation and does not accept
this element, even with zero amplitude. See the
[tracking restrictions](tracking.qmd#ring-boundary-refinement) and
[orbit handover requirements](tracking.qmd#opalx-initial-orbit).

### Time-dependence definitions {#element-time-dependence-definitions}

`POLYNOMIAL_TIME_DEPENDENCE`
: Defines $f(t)=\sum_i c_i t^i$. When used by `VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY`, time is
  in seconds, so coefficient $c_i$ has model-output units per $\mathrm{s}^i$.
  Use either `P0` through `P3`
  or `COEFFICIENTS`, not both.

`SINUSOIDAL_TIME_DEPENDENCE`
: Sums components $\tfrac{a_i}{2}\sin(2\pi f_i t + \phi_i) + o_i$. The length
  of `FREQUENCIES` sets the number of components. `PHASE_OFFSETS`, `AMPLITUDES`
  (peak-to-peak) and `DC_OFFSETS` are optional; missing entries default to 0, 1
  and 0, and extra entries are ignored. With the cavity's time in seconds, `FREQUENCIES` are in Hz;
  these are modulation frequencies, distinct from the MHz output expected
  by `FREQUENCY_MODEL`. [The current sinusoidal integral has an inconsistent
  oscillating-amplitude normalization; use a polynomial frequency model
  when the RF phase must be the integral of its specified frequency.]{#ug-12-33}

`SPLINE_TIME_DEPENDENCE`
: Interpolates `VALUES` at strictly increasing `TIMES`, in seconds when used
  by `VARIABLE_RF_CAVITY`. `ORDER=1`
  selects linear interpolation and `ORDER=3` selects cubic interpolation with
  quadratic smoothing. The `ORDER` attribute accepts only those two values.

## Current limitations {#element-limitations}

- Registration establishes accepted input syntax, not numerical validation.
  Elements without a maintained regression input are identified above.
- `QUADRUPOLE`, `MULTIPOLE`, `RBEND` and `SBEND` take their rigidity from the
  global `P0`, not from `BEAM`. Set `P0` to the beam's reference momentum.
- `RBEND` and `SBEND` apply dipole and quadrupole fields only; `K2` and `K3`
  are ignored.
- `LASER` cannot be tracked, and `MARKER` placement attributes have no effect.
- Field-map elements require their external maps; generated maps and large
  binary support data belong outside the manual repository.
- Establish step-size, placement, aperture, and field-map convergence for each
  production lattice rather than treating a regression configuration as an
  accuracy prescription.
:::
